The Sentence cards card on the home screen picks one complete sentence every day. Swipe and rate with three buttons for sentence-level memory.
One sentence a day: due sentences first; otherwise a new random sentence. Learned sentences are not repeated and new ones rotate across articles.

Three buttons at the bottom: Forgot / Hard / Remembered. Tap to move to the next card; the finish page appears after all are rated.
Ratings feed FSRS spaced repetition: forgotten sentences return soon, remembered ones at longer intervals. The Sentence memory section on the stats page shows cumulative reviews and retention.
Four modes with increasing difficulty: structure first, then details, then full recall.

To keep the interface clean, many actions have no buttons and live in long-press, pull-down and edit mode. Here is the full list.
Long-press any card to enter edit mode; tap Done at the bottom to exit.
In edit mode, drag a card to move it; use the dark handle at the bottom right to resize it larger or smaller.
In edit mode, the corner buttons are: pin or unpin, and delete the card.
The plus button at the top in edit mode opens the add-card panel: due, continue, recent articles, article card, sentence card, study data, global data, add article, custom profile.
You can add several Article cards, one per article. They are one row high by default and look like Recent; they can grow to two rows, but extra space stays empty when there is little content.
The Sentence card picks one sentence a day: due first, otherwise a new random sentence. Tap it for the large card; swipe up for the next and use the three rating buttons to advance.
The Manage recent articles entry manages reading history without affecting the articles themselves.
Keep pulling down at the top until the hint bar appears; pull until it says release (with vibration), then let go to expand the brand bar.
When the top bar is open, pull past the threshold again and release to collapse it.
A light flick does not trigger it; only the threshold counts, preventing accidental changes.
Tap the top-left icon to change the logo, including a custom emoji.
Tap the subtitle text to customise the subtitle.
Tap an article to open the reader.
Long-press for selection mode: batch delete, select 2 or more for cross-text mixed practice, or send to AI.
Bottom buttons: study stats, reading mode, custom, start practice. The Pro version also has AI.
Reading mode adjusts font size, line spacing, font, weight, colours and masking granularity: balanced, words, or custom.
Pinch the body text with two fingers to zoom the font size directly.
Top right: delete or edit the article.
Switch masking granularity to Custom to open the profile list. Tap a profile to use it; tap Edit at the end of a row to open the marking page; long-press to rename or delete.
When custom granularity is selected, the button shows the name of the profile in use.

Marking page: tap a sentence to mask the whole sentence; long-press a sentence to split it into words and tap a word to mask it; long-press a word to split it into characters; long-press again to restore level by level.
Pinch with two fingers on the marking page to zoom the body font size for precise word marking.
Top menu: switch practice mode, cloze strategy, hints, immersive mode and paragraph layers, and export a PDF paper or share notes.
Long-press a sentence or word during practice to switch cloze granularity: multi-sentence, clause, word, character, then back in a loop.
The score card after finishing shows accuracy and time, and can be shared directly.
Profile list: tap to edit; long-press to start practice, rename or delete; in picker mode, tap to start practice directly.
Edit page: tap to select blanks, long-press to switch granularity, matching reader marking.
Use Save and mark blanks on the import page to go straight to creating a profile — mark key points right after importing.
Two ways: paste text or import a file (txt, PDF, Word and more; PDF can be previewed).
If the title is left empty, you can use the suggested title extracted from the body with one tap.
Very large text is reported and truncated; split it into several imports.
Two buttons at the bottom: Save only stores and returns; Save and mark blanks stores and opens custom cloze editing for that article.
The white round button at the top left of every page goes back; the system back gesture or key also works.
When the reader is in marking or editing state, exit editing first, then leave the page.
Key actions give haptic feedback: pulling past the threshold, long-pressing into card editing, dragging or resizing a card, long-press menus and more.
Deleting an article cannot be undone: use Delete at the top right of the reader or batch delete in My articles.

Data in settings: one-tap export packs the article library and practice progress into one backup file; one-tap import restores to a new install (overwrites current data; the app exits to restart after completion).
With AI enabled, you can hand your articles to AI to explain difficult points, create exercises and analyse frequent mistakes.
Turn it on in Settings → AI → Enable AI, then fill in the API URL, API key and model name. OpenAI-compatible endpoints are supported (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi and others).
Web search: enable it in settings, register free at tavily.com with an email, copy the API key from the console (tvly-xxx, 1000 free calls per month) and paste it into the Tavily API Key field.
While reading an article, tap AI in the bottom button row to open a chat with the current article.
Send to AI in the article list
Long-press an article for selection mode, then tap Send to AI to chat with several articles across texts.
AI chat history in My articles
Appears after Save AI chats is enabled; view past conversations and continue chatting.

AI combines article content and your study data (practice count, accuracy, frequent mistakes) for targeted coaching. Long-press any message to copy it; Copy chat at the top copies the whole conversation.

After Save AI chats is enabled in settings, every conversation is stored on this device. Open AI chat history from My articles at any time; tap a conversation to continue it. Nothing new is saved after turning it off.

After enabling Web search in settings and entering a Tavily key, questions trigger an automatic web search for verification and AI prioritises authoritative results (useful for checking recitation content and exam points). Without it, AI answers only from the article and its own knowledge.

API keys are encrypted by the system and stored only on this device; they are never uploaded. Note: during a chat, article content and study data are sent to the API service you configured. After disabling AI, all AI entry points are hidden.
On the Data page, scroll to the very top and keep pulling down; when the ring is full and the phone buzzes, let go to open the study flow, the planned articles laid out in time order.
In the study flow you can pause, resume or reschedule each article; scroll to the bottom and pull up, or tap back at the top left, to return to the Data page.
